syntax.title: Basics
syntax.code:
// a comment
say "Hello", 42, true     // print values, separated by spaces
let name = "Ada"          // create a name
name = "Grace"            // change it later
say "Hi {name}, {1 + 2}"  // {…} puts values inside text
let a = 1; let b = 2     // ; also separates statements
syntax.note: One statement per line. Names use letters, digits and underscores.

syntax.title: Values
syntax.code:
42   3.14   -7           // numbers
"text"   'text'           // text (both quote styles work)
true   false               // bools
nothing                    // no value
[1, 2, 3]                  // list
{name: "Ada", age: 36}     // map
1..5                       // range (includes both ends, can count down: 5..1)
syntax.note: Falsy values: false, nothing, 0 and "". Everything else is true.

syntax.title: Operators
syntax.code:
+  -  *  /  %  **          // math (% is remainder, ** is power)
==  !=  <  <=  >  >=        // comparing
and   or   not             // logic (and / or return one of their sides)
a ?? b                     // b only when a is nothing
"a" + "b"   "ab" * 3      // join and repeat text
[1] + [2]                  // join lists
x |> f   x |> f(2)         // pipe: f(x)   f(x, 2)
x += 1   x -= 1   x *= 2   // shortcuts
syntax.note: Precedence, high to low: **, unary -, * / %, + -, .., comparisons, not, and, or, ??, |>.

syntax.title: Decisions
syntax.note: if is also a value. Conditions need no brackets.

syntax.title: Match
syntax.note: First matching line wins. A line can be a value, a statement, or a { block }.

syntax.title: Loops
syntax.note: for also walks through text, ranges and map keys.

syntax.title: Functions
syntax.code:
fn add(a, b) {
  give a + b
}
fn square(n) => n * n
fn greet(name = "friend") => "Hi {name}"
let triple = fn(x) => x * 3
say add(1, 2), square(4), greet()
syntax.note: give sends a value back. Functions can be used above the line that declares them. They can be stored, passed around and returned (closures).

syntax.title: Lists and maps
syntax.code:
let xs = [10, 20, 30]
say xs[0], xs[-1], len(xs)
xs[1] = 99
push(xs, 40)
let m = {a: 1}
m.b = 2
m["c"] = 3
say m.a, m["b"], m.missing    // missing keys give nothing
syntax.note: Lists start at position 0; negative positions count from the end. Lists and maps are shared when assigned, use copy() for an independent one.

syntax.title: Errors
syntax.note: e holds the error message as text. Runaway loops and runaway recursion cannot be caught.

syntax.title: Methods and files
syntax.code:
say "hi".upper()                 // same as upper("hi")
say [3, 1, 2].sort().reverse()
use "tools.kes"                  // load another file (command line)
syntax.note: Any built-in or function you define can be called with a dot, with the first value in front.

items.name: ask
items.desc: Reads one line of input as text. Gives nothing when the input has run out.

items.name: type
items.desc: The type as text: "number", "text", "bool", "list", "map", "function", "range" or "nothing".

items.name: str
items.desc: Turns any value into text.

items.name: num
items.desc: Turns text like "3.5" into a number. Fails if it is not a number.

items.name: int
items.desc: A number (or number-like text) with the decimals cut off.

items.name: list
items.desc: Makes a list from a range, text (its characters) or a map (its keys).

items.name: copy
items.desc: A new, independent copy of a list or map.

items.name: abs
items.desc: Distance from zero: abs(-3) is 3.

items.name: floor
items.desc: Rounds down.

items.name: ceil
items.desc: Rounds up.

items.name: sqrt
items.desc: Square root.

items.name: round
items.desc: Rounds to the nearest whole number, or to a number of decimal places.

items.name: min
items.desc: The smallest number.

items.name: max
items.desc: The largest number.

items.name: sum
items.desc: Adds up a list of numbers.

items.name: random
items.desc: A random decimal from 0 up to (not including) 1.

items.name: randomInt
items.desc: A random whole number from low to high, both included.

items.name: len
items.desc: How many items (or characters, or keys).

items.name: push
items.desc: Adds to the end of a list. Gives the list back.

items.name: pop
items.desc: Removes and gives back the last item.

items.name: remove
items.desc: Removes an item and gives it back.

items.name: slice
items.desc: A piece of a list or text. `to` is not included. Negative positions count from the end.

items.name: reverse
items.desc: A reversed copy of a list or text.

items.name: sort
items.desc: A sorted copy. With a function, sorts by what the function gives for each item.

items.name: unique
items.desc: A copy with duplicates removed.

items.name: keys
items.desc: A list of the keys.

items.name: values
items.desc: A list of the values.

items.name: entries
items.desc: A list of [key, value] pairs.

items.name: contains
items.desc: True if text contains the text x, a list holds x, a map has the key x, or a range includes x.

items.name: find
items.desc: Position of x in text or a list, or -1 when it is not there.

items.name: map
items.desc: A new list made by applying fn to every item. If fn takes two parameters it also gets the position.

items.name: filter
items.desc: Keeps the items for which fn gives something true.

items.name: reduce
items.desc: Folds a list into one value. fn gets (total so far, next item).

items.name: any
items.desc: True if fn is true for at least one item.

items.name: all
items.desc: True if fn is true for every item.

items.name: upper
items.desc: UPPER CASE.

items.name: lower
items.desc: lower case.

items.name: trim
items.desc: Removes spaces at both ends.

items.name: split
items.desc: Cuts text into a list. With no separator it splits on spaces; with "" it gives every character.

items.name: join
items.desc: Glues the items of a list into one text.

items.name: replace
items.desc: Replaces every old with new.

items.name: startsWith
items.desc: True if the text begins with start.

items.name: endsWith
items.desc: True if the text ends with end.

items.name: repeat
items.desc: The text repeated. Same as text * times.

items.name: assert
items.desc: Does nothing when the condition is true. Fails with the message when it is false.
